extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — applicants, reviewers, and NIH review staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and description of NIH's consolidation of peer review within CSR, including how applications will be grouped, study sections chartered, reviewers recruited, and review practices standardized to improve efficiency, competition, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency and cost savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralizing peer review allowed for cost savings through increased efficiency; per application review costs were much lower at CSR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management and support of peer review require fewer staff; larger, more efficient study sections and larger meetings make more efficient use of staff and reviewer effort. The consolidation reflects economies of scale and reduces per-application cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of review practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralization allows for consistency in review practices across NIH; while all NIH review branches followed the same review policies there was significant local variation in review practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSR developed standard guidelines for conducting the review of career development, training, and multicomponent grants. Review procedures were standardized and implemented via staff and reviewer training to reduce local variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximizing scientific competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Having review meetings with applications grouped according to science, rather than the IC that administers them, promotes appropriate competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouping by scientific topic is intended to 'maximize scientific competition to better identify the most innovative ideas' and should result in better review outcomes by exposing proposals to a broader, topical peer set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictable, transparent review homes
rubrics_metrics.description: Create stable, predictable, and transparent review homes for grant applications absorbed by CSR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSR expects to create 52 new chartered study sections; descriptions for new study sections are posted on NIH’s website to provide transparency about where and how applications will be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate clustering by review criteria and scientific area
rubrics_metrics.description: Special emphasis panels will cluster applications with similar review criteria and in similar scientific areas to ensure that the applications are evaluated appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each of the five scientific review divisions within CSR has established recurring panels for career development, institutional training, and multicomponent applications so that applications with similar criteria are reviewed together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and recruitment of reviewer expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: CSR is recruiting reviewers who had previously served on panels convened by funding ICs to retain valuable expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining continuity of expertise from IC-run panels is an explicit objective; active recruitment and outreach to prior reviewers supports institutional knowledge and review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and continuing education for review staff and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Training of staff and reviewers is necessary to effectively implement standard review practices and to implement new review practices, such as the Simplified Review Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSR centralized training resources allowing all NIH scientific review officers to participate in interactive trainings; robust training and continuing education efforts are in place to support consistent implementation of policies and new practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized decision-making and policy management
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralized decision-making and policy management is more efficient and faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central policy management enabled a rapid NIH response to operational disruptions (e.g., lapse in appropriations) and supports quicker, coordinated decisions across review operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational resilience and ability to respond to emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Having all peer review operations within CSR allowed a quick and decisive response to the 43-day lapse in appropriations in 2025, enabling CSR to complete a review round rather than cancel it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralization is framed as improving NIH's ability to maintain review cycles under stress; operational continuity is a performance objective for the consolidated system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating appropriately sized and focused study sections
rubrics_metrics.description: CSR expects to create 52 new chartered study sections; these study sections are being created out of existing study sections, which are now oversubscribed. Overflowing study sections will be divided to cover different, scientifically coherent sets of topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study sections should be sized and scoped to be scientifically coherent and manageable, splitting oversubscribed sections into distinct topic-focused sections to ensure appropriate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of recurring special emphasis panels for non-R01 applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the five scientific review divisions has established recurring special emphasis panels to review career development, institutional training, and multicomponent program project applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recurring panels cluster similar application types to ensure consistent application of review criteria and appropriate scientific context for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to rigorous, fair, and transparent review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH remains committed to ensuring rigorous, fair, and transparent review as policies, procedures, and structures continue to evolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overarching standard guides centralization decisions, standard-setting, training, reviewer recruitment, and public posting of study section descriptions; transparency and fairness are explicit goals of the restructured system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of new review practices (e.g., Simplified Review Framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement new review practices, such as the Simplified Review Framework, as part of standardization efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New practices require training and consistent rollout across CSR-managed reviews; their adoption is cited as a substantive change necessitating staff and reviewer education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping applications by science rather than administrative IC
rubrics_metrics.description: Free of the constraint of administrative assignments, applications can be grouped together based on science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operational principle underlies study section creation and clustering and is intended to improve scientific coherence and competition in review meetings.
